plan.title: Create Configuration Module
plan.description: Create Configuration Module: Create a configuration module (e.g., 'config.py') that defines application settings such as decimal precision, error handling behavior for division by zero, and other operational parameters.
plan.verification: Verify that the configuration module can be imported and returns the expected default settings.

plan.title: Create Calculator Module
plan.description: Create Calculator Module: Create a calculator module (e.g., 'calc.py') implementing basic arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) that respects the settings defined in the configuration module.
plan.verification: Verify that the calculator functions execute correctly and apply the configuration settings (e.g., rounding to the specified decimal precision).

plan.title: Create Unit Tests
plan.description: Create Unit Tests: Write a comprehensive suite of unit tests to validate the calculator's arithmetic operations, edge cases (such as division by zero), and configuration integration.
plan.verification: Run the test suite and ensure all test cases pass successfully.

state.architecture:
Title: Calculator and Configuration Modules Design
Summary: Design and implement a modular calculator utility and a dedicated calculator configuration module in TypeScript to align with the existing repository stack. This avoids naming collisions with the main API configuration and ensures robust, configurable arithmetic operations with comprehensive unit tests.
Components:
- [NEW] CalculatorConfig: A configuration module for the calculator utility, defining settings such as decimal precision and division-by-zero behavior. (Responsibilities: Define the CalculatorConfig interface containing precision and divisionByZeroBehavior., Export a default configuration object., Provide a mechanism to dynamically update configuration options at runtime.)
- [NEW] Calculator: A utility module implementing basic arithmetic operations that dynamically respect the CalculatorConfig settings. (Responsibilities: Implement add, subtract, multiply, and divide operations., Apply decimal precision rounding to all operation results based on current configuration., Handle division-by-zero scenarios dynamically based on configuration.)
- [NEW] CalculatorTests: A comprehensive unit test suite to validate calculator operations, edge cases, and configuration integration. (Responsibilities: Verify basic arithmetic operations., Verify that precision rounding is correctly applied according to configuration., Verify division-by-zero behavior under different configuration modes., Verify dynamic configuration updates affect subsequent calculations correctly.)
Data Flow: Application or test suite imports Calculator and CalculatorConfig. -> Application configures CalculatorConfig. -> Application calls Calculator operations. -> Calculator reads current settings from CalculatorConfig. -> Calculator performs operation, applies precision rounding, and returns the result. -> Calculator handles edge cases like division by zero based on the active configuration.
Dependencies: TypeScript environment, Existing test runner configured in the repository
Risks: Naming collision with the existing 'apps/api/config.ts' if not uniquely named (mitigated by naming it 'calcConfig.ts').; Language mismatch if Python was strictly required, though TypeScript is chosen here to match the existing codebase.; Shared global state risk if configuration is modified globally in a concurrent environment.
Verification Plan: Execute the unit test suite using the project's test command.; Verify that all test cases for addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division pass.; Verify that changing the precision configuration dynamically changes the rounding behavior of the calculator.; Verify that changing the division-by-zero configuration dynamically changes the error handling behavior.

history.architecture:
Title: Calculator and Configuration Modules Design
Summary: Design and implement a modular calculator utility and a dedicated calculator configuration module in TypeScript to align with the existing repository stack. This avoids naming collisions with the main API configuration and ensures robust, configurable arithmetic operations with comprehensive unit tests.
Components:
- [NEW] CalculatorConfig: A configuration module for the calculator utility, defining settings such as decimal precision and division-by-zero behavior. (Responsibilities: Define the CalculatorConfig interface containing precision and divisionByZeroBehavior., Export a default configuration object., Provide a mechanism to dynamically update configuration options at runtime.)
- [NEW] Calculator: A utility module implementing basic arithmetic operations that dynamically respect the CalculatorConfig settings. (Responsibilities: Implement add, subtract, multiply, and divide operations., Apply decimal precision rounding to all operation results based on current configuration., Handle division-by-zero scenarios dynamically based on configuration.)
- [NEW] CalculatorTests: A comprehensive unit test suite to validate calculator operations, edge cases, and configuration integration. (Responsibilities: Verify basic arithmetic operations., Verify that precision rounding is correctly applied according to configuration., Verify division-by-zero behavior under different configuration modes., Verify dynamic configuration updates affect subsequent calculations correctly.)
Data Flow: Application or test suite imports Calculator and CalculatorConfig. -> Application configures CalculatorConfig. -> Application calls Calculator operations. -> Calculator reads current settings from CalculatorConfig. -> Calculator performs operation, applies precision rounding, and returns the result. -> Calculator handles edge cases like division by zero based on the active configuration.
Dependencies: TypeScript environment, Existing test runner configured in the repository
Risks: Naming collision with the existing 'apps/api/config.ts' if not uniquely named (mitigated by naming it 'calcConfig.ts').; Language mismatch if Python was strictly required, though TypeScript is chosen here to match the existing codebase.; Shared global state risk if configuration is modified globally in a concurrent environment.
Verification Plan: Execute the unit test suite using the project's test command.; Verify that all test cases for addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division pass.; Verify that changing the precision configuration dynamically changes the rounding behavior of the calculator.; Verify that changing the division-by-zero configuration dynamically changes the error handling behavior.
